parameters.text:
=Write an analytic briefing on the topic, using ONLY the sources provided. Style: IC analytic product. Length: 150-250 words.

Requirements:
- Cite sources using [Source N] inline markers and a numbered Sources section at the end.
- Express likelihood using one of: almost no chance / very unlikely / unlikely / roughly even chance / likely / very likely / almost certain.
- Distinguish information from judgment with explicit phrases ("we assess", "we judge", "the source reports").
- Note one alternative hypothesis where appropriate.
- Address customer relevance briefly at the end.

Topic: {{ $('Set Input').item.json.topic }}

Sources:
{{ $json.sources.map((s, i) => '[Source ' + (i+1) + '] ' + s.title + ': ' + s.extract).join('\n\n') }}

=You are an IC analytic-product auditor. Audit the briefing below against four policies (provided after the briefing). For each rule that is violated or of concern, produce a finding:

- Citation: <ICD-XXX> / <rule name>
- Severity: violation | concern | compliant
- Quote: <exact phrase from briefing>
- Explanation: <why it violates the rule>
- Fix: <what to change>

Only flag issues grounded in a specific rule cited verbatim from the policies below. Do NOT invent rules. Do not flag stylistic preferences not in the policies.

If the briefing is fully compliant, output exactly: COMPLIANT

If there are findings, list them, then end with one summary line:
SUMMARY: <N> findings, <V> violations.

BRIEFING:
{{ $('Synthesise Briefing').item.json.text }}

POLICIES (simplified):

ICD-203 / Analytic Standards. Key rules: objective; independent of political consideration; timely; based on all available sources; expresses-uncertainty (use one likelihood scale; do not mix likelihood with confidence in same sentence); distinguishes-information-from-judgment; analysis-of-alternatives; clear-argumentation; change-or-consistency; accurate-judgments.

ICD-206 / Sourcing. Key rules: SRC required when source cited or judgment depends on source; source descriptors describe credibility, bias, age, expertise; source summary statements encouraged for complex products.

ICD-208 / Maximising Utility. Key rules: know-your-customers; meet-analytic-standards (per ICD-203); produce-for-tailored-reuse; discoverable-and-accessible; demonstrate-transparency.

ICS-206-1 / PAI/CAI/OSINT/AI Citation. Key rules: cite AI when value-added; for generative-AI cite platform AND full prompt text; for classification-models cite model name + precision/recall + training data + version; commercial tools cited if value-added analytics.

nodes.name: Final lab — all four patterns combined

parameters.content:
## Ex 07 — Research Agent (Final Lab)

This workflow is the integration exercise. It uses **all four patterns** from the slides:

```
Topic ─→ Generate Query ─→ Wikipedia Search ─→ Split Hits ─→ Fetch Summary  ─→ Aggregate ─→ Synthesise Briefing ─→ Audit Briefing ─→ Audit Clean? ─┬─ yes ─→ Final (Approved)
         (Chaining)        (HTTP)              (Parallel-ish:    (× 3)         (Aggregate)   (Chaining)             (Evaluator)         (Routing/Gate)    └─ no ─→ Revise → Final (Revised)
                                                Wikipedia returns                                                                                                  (Optimiser)
                                                3 hits, each gets
                                                its own Fetch call)
```

**Why the audit step is the lesson.** A draft from an LLM is not a finished product. The audit step encodes a *policy* — the four ICD standards in `policies/` — and refuses to let non-compliant output through. The same shape applies to any organisation with a published style guide, brand voice, regulatory standard, or quality bar.

## The audit step

The Audit Briefing prompt embeds a *summary* of the four ICD policies. Full policy XML lives in `policies/ICD-203.xml`, `ICD-206.xml`, `ICD-208.xml`, `ICS-206-1.xml`.

Read them. Compare to the prompt summary. The summary captures the rule names that the auditor LLM uses to ground its findings.

For a more thorough audit, paste the full XML of all four policies into the Audit Briefing prompt instead of the summary. Tradeoff: latency goes up, accuracy goes up.
